title: Stability sprint communique - Nov 25 2029
content:
Quick summary

This note captures the SRE stability sprint highlights for the week of 2029-11-18 -> 2029-11-24. Focus areas: SLA risk from two repeated degradations, a persistent KV cache eviction pattern affecting tail-latency on long-context workloads, and tuning the Dedicated autoscaler for multi-tenant GPU pools. This doc is intentionally concise — action owners listed at the bottom.

Incident snapshots (high level)

1) KV-cache tail-latency spikes (Nov 19, partial recurrence Nov 22)
- Symptom: 95th/99th generation latency increased by 2.4–3.1x on long-context (>2k tokens) requests for a subset of model shards. Observed as elevated retry counts and client-side timeouts.
- Impact: ~0.6% of hosted-api requests, primarily heavy-chat customers on hosted tier; a few Dedicated routes also observed degraded percentiles due to shared KV-mesh. No data loss.
- Detection: spike alerted by latency-scan and validated from tracing (trace sample INF-2029-11-19-KV).
- Root cause hypothesis: aggressive cache compaction/eviction triggered by a change in our background reclaimer (runtime PR 1187) combined with slightly higher-than-expected concurrent KV warm-ups from a scheduled evaluation job.
- Short-term mitigations applied: rolled back reclaimer tweak (runtime PR revert), temporarily increased cache capacity on affected nodes, added a circuit to throttle concurrent KV warm-up jobs.
- Next steps (owner): Diego — complete postmortem draft by 2029-11-28 and add deterministic repro (INF-4321). Rina — run longer soak tests on canary cluster with synthetic long-context workloads.

2) Dedicated autoscaler oscillation (Nov 21)
- Symptom: autoscaler thrashing between scale-up and scale-down over a 2-hour window during a synthetic traffic spike from an internal loadtest. The oscillation caused brief scheduling delays (~10–30s) for new inference containers.
- Impact: minimal customer impact (mostly internal), exposed instability in scale decision hysteresis and burst headroom config.
- Root cause: scale-down decision considered ephemeral drop in queue depth; lack of smoothing on GPU allocation signals.
- Short-term mitigations: increased scaleDownCooldown to 3m, introduced simple smoothing on queueDepth metric, and added an interim guard to prefer keeping a single extra pod during burst windows.
- Next steps (owner): Liam — propose a more robust hysteresis algorithm and a test harness to simulate bursty arrival patterns (proposal due 2029-12-02).

Operational SLO snapshot (rolling 28d window ending 2029-11-24)
- Generation latency SLO (p50/p95/p99): 60ms / 210ms / 720ms (SLO: p95 <= 250ms). Status: at risk historically due to tail events (see KV cache incident).
- API availability: 99.991% (target 99.99%). OK.
- Embeddings throughput SLO: 98.6% of batches completed under expected token-per-second threshold (target >=99%). Action: Optimize batching window (see Optimize ticket INF-4399).

Observability & signals notes
- We added a temporary synthetic workload to exercise long-context KV paths (runs every 30m). Early signals show lower variance after mitigation but still not fully resolved.
- Traces collected from affected requests include correlation id header x-rdw-trace-id. Use tag kv-hot-path in trace queries to filter.
- Cost signal: increased cache size temporarily increased memory per node by ~7% (cost ops informed). Keep capacity bump until postmortem validated.

Runbook and playbook updates
- Runbook: kv-cache-eviction runbook updated with detection query, rollback steps, and a checklist to validate KV warm-up throttle. (Confluence page: Runbooks/kv-cache-eviction).
- Autoscaler playbook: added a temporary tuning section for cooldown windows and burst headroom; marked as experimental.

On-call handoff (what the next shift should watch)
- Watchlist for next 72 hours:
  * Any reoccurrence of kv-cache 95/99 spikes — alert: kv-tail-latency-high. If triggered, immediately pin nodes out of rotation and escalate to runtime oncall.
  * Dedicated scale oscillation — alert: autoscaler-oscillation. If recurring more than twice in 6h, switch to manual scale and notify platform-eng.
  * Embeddings backlog bump during EU morning hours — monitor embeddings-queue-depth and throttle lower-priority background jobs.
- Handoff notes from outgoing oncall (Maya): increased sampling on long-context traces, manual throttle applied to eval-job EVAL-231, and cache size bumped on A/B nodes (Asha to track rollback window).

Action items and owners
- Diego: write postmortem (initial draft 2029-11-28), attach deterministic repro and runbook links.
- Rina: run 48h soak on canary cluster with 10x long-context QPS and report variance metrics (2029-11-30).
- Liam: design hysteresis + smoothing proposal for Dedicated autoscaler and include perf benchmarks (2029-12-02).
- Asha: coordinate with finance/cost-ops about temporary memory bump and quantify cost delta (2029-11-29).
- Ops: add an automated rollback job for reclaimer PRs merged during peak hours (INF-4405).

Open questions / investigation threads
- Why did the reclaimer change interact with KV warmup in a non-linear way? (Diego & runtime team). Need a matrix of warm-up concurrency vs. eviction threshold.
- Can we expose a per-customer KV warmup budget to protect shared pools? (Product + SRE exploration).

Meeting notes / alignment items
- Sync planned with Runtime Eng + Serving on 2029-11-27, 10:00 PT. Agenda: incident recap, repro plan, long-term cache architecture options (per-tenant cache vs. smarter compaction).
- Follow-up with Product-hosted-api: share a short RCA highlight for customers affected with guidance and ETA for next update (customer comms draft by CS).

Random notes / scratchpad (informal)
- Saw an interesting trace where a single request spawned 6 warm-ups in parallel — suspect race during kv-miss path. Add logging around warmup start/finish.
- Consider adding a budget token bucket for warmups (rate limit per minute per pool).

Appendix: useful links and tickets
- INF-4321: ticket for kv-cache postmortem (Jira).
- INF-4399: batching/embeddings tuning.
- INF-4405: rollback job automation.
- Runtime PR 1187 (reclaimer tweak) and PR revert 1189.
- Confluence: Runbooks/kv-cache-eviction

End of communique — please ping in #sre-ops if you need immediate context or want to volunteer for soak testing.
